verdict.rationale: PagerDuty's own docs establish native on-call schedules that map coverage needs and feed escalation policies, so the product directly provides scheduling. However, the pack never documents the specific rotation, layer, time-zone or round-robin mechanics the story asks for, and one hands-on user reports that cross-regional and holiday scheduling were poorly implemented and needed 'overrides on top of overrides', which lowers quality without contradicting that scheduling exists. Missing for 10: documented rotation/layer configuration, time-zone handling, round-robin coverage, and independent corroboration that schedules match real team workflows.

support.subject: As an SRE, I can build on-call schedules with rotations, layers, time zones, and round-robin coverage that match how my teams actually work

citations.quote: Use legacy schedules to map your coverage needs and determine who receives a notification when an incident triggers.
connect services to individual users and/or schedules
